programme.title: Summer Night Concert from Vienna 2026
programme.desc: Petroc Trelawny presents as Bass-baritone Bryn Terfel joins guest conductor Lorenzo Viotti and the Vienna Philharmonic at Schönbrunn Palace for arias from Verdi's Falstaff and Wagner's Das Rheingold and Tevye's song from Fiddler on the Roof. Projected onto the façade of the Schönbrunn Palace, dancers from the Vienna State Ballet join the orchestra to bring the story of Daphnis and Chloé to life through the power of Ravel's music

programme.title: The Last Battle of the Vikings
programme.desc: Marine archaeologist Dr Jon Henderson tells the story of the Norsemen in Scotland, visiting archaeological sites across Scotland and Norway. He reveals that, although the battle at Largs with the Scottish army in 1263 marked the end of an era for the Norsemen, their presence continued to shape the identity and culture of the Scottish nation to the present day

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough examines a few of the millions of insect species, and illustrates how many have developed symbiotic relationships with plants in a cycle of pollination in which they might not be able to survive without each other

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Beginning at London's Marylebone railway terminus, Michael Portillo embarks on a exploration of Britain's southern counties. His first stop is Denham in Buckinghamshire, where engineers are constructing a striking new viaduct that will be the longest railway bridge in the UK, then he alights at High Wycombe, a historic centre of furniture-making thanks to its setting amid an abundance of beechwood forest

programme.title: Today at the Test
programme.desc: England v India. Action from the third day of the one-off women's Test from Lord's, London. The last time these two sides met in a Test match was in India in December 2023, when India claimed a massive 347-run victory after making scores of 428 and 186-6 declared. In reply England made just 136 in their first innings and were then bowled out for 131 in their pursuit of a highly unlikely 479 to win the game

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Pianist Martha Argerich performs Schubert's Rondo in A, with conductor Daniel Barenboim, in an extract from the 2016 Proms. Presented by Katie Derham and Samira Ahmed

programme.title: Summer Night Concert from Vienna 2026

programme.title: The Lark Ascending
programme.desc: Diana Rigg explores the enduring popularity of composer Vaughan Williams' The Lark Ascending, which was written in 1914 as Europe approached the First World War. The programme culminates in a performance by 15-year-old violinist Julia Hwang and pianist Charles Matthews at Shirehampton Public Hall, Bristol, where the piece was premiered in December 1920. Featuring contributions by actor Peter Sallis, performer Tasmin Little, and critic and friend of the composer, Michael Kennedy

programme.title: Letters from Baghdad
programme.desc: The extraordinary and dramatic story of Gertrude Bell, who helped to shape the modern Middle East after the Second World War in ways that still reverberate today. Using never-seen-before footage of the region, the film chronicles Bell's extraordinary journey into both the uncharted Arabian desert and the inner sanctum of British male colonial power

programme.title: The Man Who Discovered Egypt
programme.desc: A profile of Victorian adventurer Flinders Petrie, who changed the world's understanding of ancient Egyptian civilisation. Chris Naunton explains how Petrie conducted a scientific survey of the pyramids, making valuable historical discoveries along the way, and also reveals how Petrie's methods of investigation revolutionised archaeology

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the riches and unique legacy of Greek art, telling the story of its mysterious origins as he starts his journey at the palace of Knossos in Crete. He then travels to Santorini and finds gold in the fabled stronghold of Mycenae, and uncovers the beginnings of a defining spirit in Greek art - embracing mythology, a passion for symmetry, and an obsession with the human body

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo joins Navy Wings pilots for a close formation flight in the skies over Royal Naval Air Station Yeovilton. His 1954 Harvard single-engine aircraft is flanked by a de Havilland Chipmunk and a Supermarine Seafire. He also visits a signaling manufacturer in Wiltshire that has been at the heart of British railway projects for decades

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his tour of the southern counties by riding a 1940s steam locomotive at the Swanage Railway. In Poole, Michael discovers an icon of the 1960s, the lava lamp, which he learns was invented in the town by an accountant. At Romsey, Michael heads to the Broadlands Estate to learn about Louis Mountbatten's multiple roles and his assassination in 1979

programme.title: Today at the Test
programme.desc: England v India. Action from the fourth day of the one-off women's Test from Lord's, London. This was England's first test ever to take place at this iconic ground, and they will have been looking to mark the occasion with their first Test victory over India since 1995. The hosts were also searching for their first win in this format since December 2024, when they beat South Africa by 286 runs in Bloemfontein

programme.title: Wild Scotland

programme.title: Andy Warhol's America
programme.desc: The final episode sees a much more cautious Warhol, a man obsessed with money and security. He reflects on the upper echelons of American society, and becomes obsessed by Nixon's visit to China. He also documents the underside of US life, exiled drag queens, racism and the plight of the homeless

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: The team travels across Great Britain to investigate evidence that suggests the search for alien life may lie within Earth's own solar system. Off the east coast of Scotland, Chris Lintott meets Claire Cousins, who explains the fundamental conditions needed for life, while Maggie Aderin is in Milton Keynes to meet Mark Fox-Powell, whose team are recreating the freezing conditions of the icy moons of Jupiter and Saturn in the lab to understand how chemistry behaves there

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes focuses on work that responded to the Vietnam War and civil strife, tracing the development of minimalism and ending on top of an extinct volcano

programme.title: Stolen: Catching the Art Thieves
programme.desc: In December 2000, Renoir's Conversation and Jeune Parisienne and a Rembrandt self-portrait from 1630 were stolen at gunpoint from Stockholm's National Museum, with the three paintings valued at more more than £40million. The subsequent hunt for the culprits took investigators on a complex hunt from Russian-organised crime to the glittering hills of Hollywood involving charismatic FBI agents

programme.title: Wimbledon 2026
programme.desc: Coverage of day 14 of the Grand Slam tournament from the All England Club, where the ladies' doubles final is scheduled to take place. Veronika Kudermetova and Elise Mertens came back from a set down to overcome Hsieh Su-wei and Jelena Ostapenko in last year's showpiece match. It was Kudermetova's maiden Grand Slam title, but Mertens' fifth, and she went on to win a sixth at this year's Australian Open alongside Zhang Shuai

programme.title: Wimbledon 2026
programme.desc: Clare Balding presents further coverage of day 14 of from the All England Club, where Jannik Sinner v Alexander Zverez in the men's singles final takes centre-stage. Sinner is the reigning champion, having defeated Carlos Alcaraz in last year's final, and overcame Novak Djokovic in the last four for the second successive year. His opponent is playing in this final for the first time, but he won his maiden Grand slam title last month at Roland Garros, and comfortably defeated home favourite Arthur Fery in the semi-finals here

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: Animals that live in Asia's deserts and dry grasslands, including the Gobi bear, one of the rarest animals on Earth who communicate by leaving their scent on ancient trees. The Thar in India is the most densely populated desert in the world, and a place where Demoiselle cranes migrate thousands of miles to reach, being welcomed with grain put out by the local Jain community

programme.title: I, Jack Wright
programme.desc: Murder mystery drama about the Wright family, who are left in disarray after one of their own - Jack, a powerful and successful businessman - apparently takes his own life. When the provisions of Jack's final will and testament are made known, his third wife Sally and two sons, Gray and John, are shocked to discover they have been largely cut out of Jack's fortune. As DCI Morgan and DC Jones delve further into the case, they realise that Jack's cause of death was in fact murder. Their sights turn to the Wright family, where a feud is beginning - as each family member becomes more reckless and desperate in their bid to own a piece of Jack's legacy, dark secrets and resentments are revealed with explosive consequences.

programme.title: I, Jack Wright
programme.desc: As DCI Morgan investigates Jack's death, the dead man's third wife Sally begins the formal process of challenging the will, while Gray is pursued by loan shark Eddie. Murder mystery, starring Nikki Amuka-Bird, John Simm and Harry Lloyd

programme.title: The Notebook (2004)
programme.desc: An elderly man reads a love story to a woman in a nursing home, from an old notebook full of sentimental scribblings about passionate young couple Allie and Noah, whose fledgling affair in the 1940s is smothered almost before it has begun when Allie's parents do not approve of her partner as he does not fit in with their other wealthy friends. Romantic drama, starring Ryan Gosling, Rachel McAdams, Gena Rowlands and James Garner

Sci-fi Western, with Daniel Craig, Harrison Ford, Olivia Wilde and Sam Rockwell

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: For decades, Dubai has sold itself as a safe place to live, do business and party. But when war broke out in nearby Iran, the city's carefully curated image was shattered. Missiles and drones hit luxury hotels and critical infrastructure, ex-pats scrambled for safety, and the government clamped down on sharing images of the war. Panorama reveals through the eyes of British residents, business owners and experts how Dubai's promise of security and prosperity has been tested like never before

programme.title: Barra's Return of the Wild
programme.desc: With wildlife under threat from climate change and biodiversity crises, Barra Best meets people working to create safe spaces to help plantlife and animals thrive. In his hometown of Belfast, he finds out how one of the city's most spectacular natural phenomena was saved from extinction, then travels to the Balearic island of Ibiza where work is under way to protect their national symbol from an invading snake. Plus, the woman single-handedly protecting the fish in the canals of Leiden in the Netherlands and the hedgehog researchers hoping to solve a prickly problem in Berlin

programme.title: Location, Location, Location

programme.title: Grand Designs

With his head in the clouds and romance in the air, Bill oscillates between kitschy tourism and earnest moments with locals

programme.title: Bill Bailey Qualmpeddler

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E

programme.title: A Place in the Sun

programme.title: A Place in the Sun

programme.title: A Place in the Sun

programme.title: Immortal Egypt with Joann Fletcher
programme.desc: Archaeologist and historian Joann Fletcher explores the story of Ancient Egypt and begins with a search of the building blocks that made he civilisation so enduring. She discovers how its people changed from primitive farmers to pyramid builders in just a few centuries, and finds early evidence for Egypt's gods and its obsession with death and the afterlife. She also reveals how the first writing was used to calculate taxes and examines Egypt's first pyramid - one of the world's earliest stone structures

programme.title: Immortal Egypt with Joann Fletcher
programme.desc: The professor explores one of Saqqara's last pyramid complexes to illustrate how Ancient Egypt's 'Pyramid Age' came to an end. A worsening climate combined with political upheaval, famine and economic difficulties to plunge the state into a dark era of civil war, with the land dividing into smaller city-states headed by ambitious small-town leaders. In an obscure tomb in Thebes, she uncovers the stories of warriors who fought in the bloody battle that would eventually lead to Egypt's reunification, and reveals how settlers known as the 'Hyksos' tried to infiltrate the fledgling nation's government to seize the throne

programme.title: Immortal Egypt with Joann Fletcher
programme.desc: Joann explores the peak of ancient Egyptian civilisation by looking at the Colossi of Memnon, two massive stone statues depicting Pharaoh Amenhotep III, and examining the lives of the workers and artisans involved in the building of the Valley of the Kings. This golden age was threatened by the growing power of Karnak's priests, and Joann reveals how Tutankhamen's early death was a chance for Egypt to start afresh and rewrite history, but was undermined by decades of state-sanctioned looting of the tombs

programme.title: Immortal Egypt with Joann Fletcher
programme.desc: The historian reveals hows Egypt's enemies exploited a country weakened by internal strife, travelling south to Sudan to examine the story of the forgotten Nubian kings, who ruled Egypt from their southern homeland for a century, even building their own pyramids to bury their monarchs. She then explores how the next group of invaders the Saites took the tradition of mummification to new extremes by preserving millions of animals, before Alexander the Great came to Egypt's rescue and founded the greatest city on Earth

programme.title: WWII in Colour: Road to Victory

programme.title: Motorhoming with Merton & Webster

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer head to a secluded pike lake in Dumfries and Galloway, staying overnight at Spedlins Castle, which is reputed to be haunted. Their second fishing location at Kinmount House has a more refined feel and the boys quickly settle in to fish, discussing how Bob's life has changed since his Gone Fishing journey started so many years ago and the many beautiful places they have seen and fished

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse borrows a vintage Porsche from an old pal, so he and Bob Mortimer travel in style to the Avon in Hampshire, where they are fishing for roach, dace and river carp - a species they have yet to target. During the trip, Bob Mortimer makes the most of their treehouse accommodation and Ted has a blind date with a Patterdale called Effie - so the duo give the terrier a pep talk on the does and don'ts of doggie dating

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer venture to Sutton Lake, a sequestered lake in Shropshire, where they have their eyes set on catching a crucian carp. This is the duo's second attempt to net the elusive fish and they are changing tactics - staying overnight in bivvies in the hope of guaranteeing success. Away from the angling, the duo reminisce about vintage music and old relatives and find time for a trip to the pub

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: The friends head to the tidal outcrop of Burgh Island on the south coast of Devon to fish for wrasse, and Bob kickstarts their trip with a huge surprise for Paul. Keen to test the surrounding waters, Paul walks down to the beach, but is met with an unexpected but familiar face, while he also encounters a rather unconventional fishing approach. Will he be tempted to stray from his tried and tested methods?

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul return to the Peak District, this time with Ted, where they filmed their first episode of Gone Fishing six years ago. They start by fishing in the Wye at Haddon Hall, which was built in the 11th century and has been visited by countless kings and queens, with Paul on a quest to catch a rainbow trout. They then head off to the Derwent, where they compare their and Ted's health to that of the UK's rivers

programme.desc: The presenter examines the social significance of cars in the 20th century. programme.title: Guy Martin: Proper Jobs

programme.title: Motorhoming with Merton & Webster
programme.desc: Paul Merton and Suki Webster explore Devon, beginning by heading to Dartmoor national park to meet a local guide for a Sherlock Holmes-themed tour, as It was in the national park that Arthur Conan Doyle was inspired to write The Hound of the Baskervilles. Paul and Suki also meet Kate and Norman, who are part of the Wheeled Access group, which encourages anyone with a disability to get out and enjoy the area

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer head to Mid-Wales to fish for chub in the Irfon and Wye rivers. The friends also meet David Lyons, the founder of charity Tackling Minds, which helps people with depression, anxiety or who are recovering from addiction to get out to rivers and lakes to fish

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer head to a secluded pike lake in Dumfries and Galloway, staying overnight at Spedlins Castle, which is reputed to be haunted. Their second fishing location at Kinmount House has a more refined feel and the boys quickly settle in to fish, discussing how Bob's life has changed since his Gone Fishing journey started so many years ago and the many beautiful places they have seen and fished

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse borrows a vintage Porsche from an old pal, so he and Bob Mortimer travel in style to the Avon in Hampshire, where they are fishing for roach, dace and river carp - a species they have yet to target. During the trip, Bob Mortimer makes the most of their treehouse accommodation and Ted has a blind date with a Patterdale called Effie - so the duo give the terrier a pep talk on the does and don'ts of doggie dating

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer venture to Sutton Lake, a sequestered lake in Shropshire, where they have their eyes set on catching a crucian carp. This is the duo's second attempt to net the elusive fish and they are changing tactics - staying overnight in bivvies in the hope of guaranteeing success. Away from the angling, the duo reminisce about vintage music and old relatives and find time for a trip to the pub

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: The friends head to the tidal outcrop of Burgh Island on the south coast of Devon to fish for wrasse, and Bob kickstarts their trip with a huge surprise for Paul. Keen to test the surrounding waters, Paul walks down to the beach, but is met with an unexpected but familiar face, while he also encounters a rather unconventional fishing approach. Will he be tempted to stray from his tried and tested methods?

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul return to the Peak District, this time with Ted, where they filmed their first episode of Gone Fishing six years ago. They start by fishing in the Wye at Haddon Hall, which was built in the 11th century and has been visited by countless kings and queens, with Paul on a quest to catch a rainbow trout. They then head off to the Derwent, where they compare their and Ted's health to that of the UK's rivers

programme.title: Wild West: America's Great Frontier
programme.desc: Documentary exploring the history and geography of America's deserts, canyons and wilderness, exploring the lives of the people and animals that have found ways to thrive and prosper in these brutally inhospitable conditions. The first programme examines the agricultural traditions of the Hopi Native American tribe in northeastern Arizona, as well as exploring the strategies used by a variety of wildlife, including mustangs, coyotes and desert tortoises, to survive in these demanding environments

programme.title: Wild West: America's Great Frontier
programme.desc: Wildlife in America's mountain regions, including the Rockies and the Sierra Nevada, areas infamous for extremes of temperature from freezing winters to scorching summers. The programme examines the survival strategies employed by animals including black bears, pikas and bison, as well as parasitic plants. Plus, a look at the challenges faced by these region's human inhabitants, including ranchers leading their cattle on 70-mile journeys

programme.title: Wild West: America's Great Frontier
programme.desc: A journey along America's West coast. The programme examines how the landscape is shaped by the Pacific Ocean as well as powerful forces beneath ground, particularly along the San Andreas Fault. The programme also visits the warm and sheltered waters of the Sea of Cortez, where animals including blue whales gather, and discovers how a small community in America's westernmost point have a unique relationship with grey whales

programme.title: Alaska: Earth's Frozen Kingdom

programme.title: The Green Planet

Proboscis monkeys are forced to venture uncomfortably closer to humans, and swifts in Jerusalem face tough competition for nest sites

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: Animals that live in Asia's deserts and dry grasslands, including the Gobi bear, one of the rarest animals on Earth who communicate by leaving their scent on ancient trees. programme.title: Asia
